$schema-note: Deterministic asset budgets for issue #33. All limits are RAW bytes (uncompressed file size) measured from the production `astro build` output by web/tests/build/asset-budgets.test.ts. Raw bytes are gated because, for a given source tree, they are identical on any machine -- no compressor, so no zlib/brotli version variance. (Two pages, home and compare, stamp the build date via `new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)`, a fixed-width 10-char field: its byte LENGTH is stable across days even though its content is not, so the budgeted number does not move with the calendar.) gzip and brotli are reported by `npm run assets:report` for realism but never gated. There is no override, skip or force flag; an intentional exception is an explicit entry here with a stated reason, which is reviewable, never a bypass.
headroom-note: Ceilings sit ~12-26% above the value measured when they were set, leaving room for normal catalog growth while still reddening on a real regression -- and because a raw-byte budget is a claim about the whole built tree, it goes stale on any markup or data change by anyone, which no file-collision check can detect. The measured baseline for each entry is recorded in `measuredRaw` so the headroom is auditable. The ceilings were raised (home, catalog, updates, providers) for three causes measured earlier: the BASE_PATH=/ModelTree/ pin (+380..+5449 per route, the deploy prefix CI applies that a local root build did not), #634's SEO head markup (canonical, robots, 9 Open Graph + 5 Twitter tags, small inline JSON-LD, on every route), and #647's variant-positioning dataset plus expanded LineageExplorer/ModelPassport inlining more per-model tier data. Re-baselined on 2026-08-31 against trunk 7c506bd1 (the current rebased merge-base). Two prior re-baselines are folded into the measured values: #665 (long-tail family depth, +728..+7790 HTML) and then the 7-commit span 356989e9..7c506bd1, whose only structural mover is #674 (render EVERY cited source for a variant-positioning record, not just the first): #674 added ~16 lines to global.css (+117 raw CSS on every route, since the stylesheet is shared) and multi-source HTML to the lineage/variant routes (home +1472, tree/compare +617 each; providers +280 incl. a +165 shared-JS re-chunk from LineageExplorer.tsx). #675 nudged providers/[slug].astro (+4 lines, net ~0). The five data/test-only commits (#668/#671/#673/#676/#680) net near-zero rendered bytes. Every one of these was absorbed within existing headroom, so NO ceiling changed on this re-baseline and each `reason` records where the growth landed.
drift-note: RE-BASELINED 2026-09-02 for #813 against this branch merged with trunk 8e8ae6f9, which is the state CI builds for a pull request and the state `main` holds after the merge -- so every `measuredRaw` below is the figure that build actually produces. It was not before: the recorded values had been left at their 2026-08-31 baseline while 23 commits of data and markup landed on top, so EVERY route's recorded figure understated the truth -- tree by 75,608 bytes (677,003 recorded against 752,611 measured, 11.2%), home by 46,854, catalog by 28,502, benchmarks by 17,969, compare by 22,791, updates by 12,378, the worst passport page by 7,591 and the worst provider page by 5,837. No ceiling was ever breached, so nothing failed; `measuredRaw` is documentation, not enforcement, and the test asserts `criticalMaxRaw`. That is precisely why the drift was expensive rather than harmless -- it caused no red build and it quietly told anyone sizing a change that /tree had 82,997 bytes to spend when it had 7,389, which is what made a fully-researched data tranche look unaffordable (#811). Documentation that no test reads is documentation that decays, so `measuredDrift` below is now checked: asset-budgets.test.ts asserts every recorded measurement stays within `maxFraction` of the build's real figure, and a data tranche that outgrows it must re-run `npm run assets:report` and re-record these numbers rather than let them rot. That is a tightening and never a bypass -- the ceilings are untouched and still enforced exactly as before. RE-RECORDED 2026-09-03 for #822 against this branch merged with trunk 34e78d1a -- the state CI builds for PR #830 (web-ci.yml runs `actions/checkout@v4` on a `pull_request` with no `ref:` override, so it builds `refs/pull/830/merge`, the head merged with the base) and the state `main` holds once this lands, so every measured figure below is again the build's real output. This is the FIRST re-record the guard itself forced, and its lesson is accumulation: the #813 figures were taken against the branch merged with 8e8ae6f9, and two independently-tolerable drifts then piled on top -- #822's data tranche (one family, three releases) on this branch, and trunk's #826 (shareable lineage trails: +259 lines to LineageExplorer.tsx, +166 to global.css) which CI's merge ref builds into the tree/compare islands and the shared stylesheet. Each drift sat UNDER the 2% guard alone (a branch-only build measured tree 542692, 1.94% over the recorded 532352; trunk on its own was green too), but their SUM did not: the merge measures tree 544346 (2.25%) and compare 766171 (2.16%), which is what reddened web-ci. So neither #822 nor #826 is individually at fault -- the guard caught accumulated staleness that no single change owns, which is exactly its purpose. No ceiling moved and none came close. PROSE FIGURES, 2026-09-05 (#941): the `Attribution (measured at 95f731ab ...)` clauses below each stated the shared global stylesheet as `102872 raw bytes`; the QA gate reviewing them measured 102812, and the 60-byte disagreement outlived the issue that raised it. Adjudicated by building 95f731ab itself under the pinned deploy environment: `_astro/` emits exactly TWO stylesheets, `BaseLayout.BuORDO_x.css` at 102872 and a `/methodology`-only `methodology.CaJblxSL.css` at 4668, and 177 of the 178 built pages link the first ALONE -- so 102872 was right. The obvious hypothesis, that one side totalled whole-build `_astro/` CSS, is REFUTED: that total is 107540 and matches neither figure. 102812 is the SAME file at the SAME commit built WITHOUT the `BASE_PATH=/ModelTree/` pin -- the stylesheet carries six `url()` font references, the deploy prefix adds 10 bytes to each, and re-inserting it into the ambient build reproduces the pinned file byte-for-byte. Both sides measured correctly and the prose was under-specified: a raw byte figure is pinned by a commit AND a build environment, and the clause named only the first. That is the trap `headroom-note` above already records one level up (the deploy prefix CI applies that a local root build did not), noted there against route totals and unnoticed here inside a stylesheet figure. The raw figure is therefore REMOVED from all four clauses and the hedged proportions kept. Nothing re-measures a number in a sentence: `measuredDrift` compares fields, not prose, no field records per-route CSS, and adding one would be a structural change ADR 0015 puts OUT of class -- so the fix is to stop publishing the figure, not to guard it. `npm run assets:report` re-derives it on demand (it prints `css` raw per route), and naming the instrument beats freezing its output, because a command cannot go stale. The proportions were never in doubt: catalog reads 16.46% CSS on the pinned build and 16.46% on the ambient one, so the `~16%` survives a disagreement that took two builds to settle. Note what is NOT being deprecated here -- a figure bound to a named commit as HISTORY, every `+117`, `+1509` and `75,608` in these notes and the counts in this paragraph among them, stays true and is what these notes are for. It is the present-tense claim about what a shared asset IS that decays. Ceilings, `maxFraction` and every `measuredRaw` are untouched.

measuredDrift.reason: How far a recorded `measuredRaw`/`measuredWorst*`/`*MeasuredRaw` may sit from the figure the production build actually produces before the test reddens. 2% is chosen against the drift it exists to catch, not picked round: the 2026-09-02 re-baseline found the eight recorded figures 0.93% to 11.17% stale, and a 5% tolerance would have caught exactly ONE of them (tree, 11.17%) while home (4.83%), catalog (4.92%), the worst passport page (4.66%), benchmarks (4.04%), compare (3.13%) and updates (2.89%) all rotted on unnoticed -- six of the eight, including the two whose staleness misled #811. 2% catches seven of the eight; only the worst provider page (0.93%) sits under it, and a figure that close is not yet lying about what a change can afford. The tolerance is a FRACTION OF THE RECORDED VALUE with no absolute floor, so `measuredWorstJsRaw: 0` means exactly 0: that entry is the static-hydration tripwire and a page that starts shipping any island JS should have to say so here, over and above the separate `jsMaxRaw` ceiling. Raw bytes are deterministic for a given source tree (see the $schema-note), so this cannot flake; a failure always means the recorded number is wrong and re-recording it is the fix. Re-record with `npm run assets:report`. This guard never permits more bytes -- exceeding a ceiling still fails on the ceiling.
